findings.failure_mode: missing file, permission denied, or unreadable path panics the caller instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and use .map_err(|e| LoadError::Io(e)) or an equivalent typed error

findings.failure_mode: non-numeric, empty, or out-of-range value in column 2 panics the caller instead of returning a typed Parse/Invalid error

findings.problem: lossy cast from u32 to u16 via as — parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16
findings.failure_mode: values 65536..u32::MAX silently truncate to u16, producing incorrect records without any error
findings.fix: parse directly as u16: parts[1].parse::<u16>().map_err(|_| RecordError::InvalidValue), or use u16::try_from with checked conversion

findings.problem: parts[0] — unchecked indexing into split result
findings.failure_mode: a line with zero or one comma-delimited fields causes index-out-of-bounds panic
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',').ok_or(RecordError::InvalidLine) and bind (_name, value_str) or .get(0)/.get(1) with checked access

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) inside the mapping closure — stdout I/O in what should be a pure data pipeline
findings.failure_mode: side effects are hidden inside an iterator chain, making the function non-deterministic, untestable in isolation, and producing console spam when called from a library consumer
findings.fix: remove all println! from the core pipeline; log at the shell boundary (caller of load_sensors) or return metadata alongside records

findings.problem: load_sensors mixes file I/O (fs::read_to_string), stdout I/O (println!), and data parsing in one function
findings.failure_mode: cannot unit-test the parsing logic in isolation; cannot swap the I/O layer; violates pure-core / imperative-shell separation
findings.fix: split into (a) fn read_file(path: &str) -> Result<String, IoError>, (b) fn parse_records(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, RecordError>, and a shell fn load_sensors that wires them together

findings.problem: Vec<String> collected from line.split(',') with no try_reserve and no max-items guard
findings.failure_mode: an extremely long line or unbounded input can allocate unbounded memory; no OOM error is returned
findings.fix: use split_once for the single-comma grammar; if Vec is needed, call values.try_reserve(max_items).map_err(|_| RecordError::Allocation) and enforce max_items before pushing

findings.problem: No domain error enum exists — failures (Io, Parse, Invalid, Overflow, Allocation) are all expressed via panic
findings.failure_mode: callers cannot distinguish or handle failure modes programmatically; every error is a crash
findings.fix: define an enum RecordError { Io(std::io::Error), InvalidLine, InvalidValue, Allocation } and return Result<Vec<Record>, RecordError>

findings.problem: Record fields are pub String / pub u16 — callers can construct invalid records directly with no validation
findings.failure_mode: illegal states (empty name, negative-or-out-of-range value) are representable at compile time
findings.fix: make Record fields private, use newtypes for Name (non-empty string wrapper), and provide a fallible constructor fn Record::try_new(name: &str, value: u16) -> Result<Record, RecordError>

The crate contains multiple unwrap() calls on I/O and parse results, a lossy u32-to-u16 cast, unchecked indexing, hidden println! side effects inside an iterator, no typed error domain, no bounded allocation, and no benchmarks.
